title: Print4Kids: 3D-Printed Prednisolone Tablets in Pediatrics – Taste Masking and Improved Acceptance
summary:
Prednisolone is a medication commonly used in children and adolescents. The standard tablets have a rather bitter taste, which is why many children and adolescents are reluctant to take them. Using a 3D printer, we can now produce tablets with customized dosages. This allows us to precisely adjust the amount of the active ingredient and improve the taste. Previously, it was often necessary to split several tablets or use a liquid form to achieve the correct dose.
We are comparing two different tablets, both produced using the 3D printer: standard prednisolone tablets and tablets containing a different form of prednisolone (prednisolone disodium dihydrogen phosphate—this form is naturally less bitter).
We want to find out which tablet tastes best and is easiest to swallow. This will allow us to produce medications in the future that children are more willing to take—which is important for the treatment to be effective.
conditions: Improvement of Corticosteroid therapy for immunological/hematological disorders (ALL)/ juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA)

interventions.name: Observational study: age-appropriate survey following the administration of 3D-printed tablets (two versions in different orders) compared to standard medication

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with a prescription for oral prednisolone (2 mg or more)
Exclusion criteria:
Known intolerance to one or more of the ingredients in the 3D-printed tablets; Age < 1 year
(Ingredients in CuraBlend base: Purified water, xylitol, gelatin, cocoa butter, glycerol 85%, maltodextrin, silicon dioxide, citric acid monohydrate, sodium citrate, vanilla flavor, potassium sorbate, raspberry flavor, sucralose)
